key_insight: Oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group metal oxides track cation reducibility and can be predicted using just crystal reduction potential and band gap.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-property predictions could accelerate oxide screening for solid-oxide fuel cells and solar thermochemical fuel production.
method: Survey 39 oxide polymorphs with r²SCAN density functional theory.
Use ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral oxygen vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model using pristine-bulk descriptors.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, while the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: The largest prediction residuals occur where electron accommodation departs from the model’s cation-reduction picture.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
